2) require-story-annotation (function-level @story) - Rule: src/rules/require-story-annotation.ts - meta.messages.missingStory = "Function '{{name}}' must have an explicit @story annotation. Add a JSDoc or line comment with @story that points to the implementing story file (for example, docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md)." - meta.hasSuggestions = true, meta.fixable = "code" - Helper: src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts - reportMissing(context, sourceCode, node, passedTarget?): - Computes functionName via extractName(...) - Skips reporting if hasStoryAnnotation(sourceCode, node) is true - Resolves target for fix via resolveTargetNode(...) - Calls context.report({ node: nameNode, messageId: 'missingStory', data: { name, functionName: name }, fix: createAddStoryFix(resolvedTarget), suggest: [{ desc: "Add JSDoc @story annotation for function 'NAME', e.g., /** @story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md */", fix: createAddStoryFix(resolvedTarget) }] }) - Test: tests/rules/error-reporting.test.ts - Manually invokes rule.create(context) listeners on a synthetic AST for function bar() - Asserts exactly one report descriptor - Verifies: - rule.meta.messages.missingStory is a non-empty string containing "{{name}}" - error.messageId === 'missingStory' - error.data === { name: 'bar', functionName: 'bar' } - error.suggest[0].desc matches the expected suggestion string and has a defined fix
3) require-req-annotation (function-level @req) - Rule: src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts - meta.messages.missingReq = "Function '{{functionName}}' is missing a required @req annotation. Add a JSDoc or line comment with @req (for example, '@req REQ-EXAMPLE') referencing the appropriate requirement from the story file." - Uses checkReqAnnotation(context, node, { enableFix: false }) - Helper: src/utils/annotation-checker.ts - reportMissing(context, node, enableFix = true): - Derives name via getNodeName(node) with fallback '(anonymous)' - Selects nameNode (id/key/node) - Calls context.report({ node: nameNode, messageId: 'missingReq', data: { name, functionName: name }, ...(optional fix) }) - Adds fix when enableFix is true using createMissingReqFix(node) - Tests: tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts - File header references story 007.0 and REQ-ERROR-SPECIFIC - All invalid cases assert errors like { messageId: 'missingReq', data: { name: '', functionName: '' } } across decls, exprs, methods, and TS nodes
4) require-branch-annotation (branch-level annotations) - Rule: src/rules/require-branch-annotation.ts - meta.messages.missingAnnotation = "Branch is missing required annotation: {{missing}}." - Helper: src/utils/branch-annotation-helpers.ts - reportMissingStory(...) reports missingAnnotation with data { missing: '@story' } and optional fixer that inserts "// @story .story.md" above the branch - reportMissingReq(...) reports missingAnnotation with data { missing: '@req' } and optional fixer inserting "// @req " - reportMissingAnnotations(...) drives both story and req reporting, using consistent messageId and data shape - Tests: tests/rules/require-branch-annotation.test.ts - Header includes @story docs/stories/007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING.story.md and REQ-ERROR-SPECIFIC / REQ-ERROR-CONSISTENCY - Invalid cases assert: - errors: [{ messageId: 'missingAnnotation', data: { missing: '@story' } }, { messageId: 'missingAnnotation', data: { missing: '@req' } }] - output with inserted annotations, verifying suggestions/fixes and concrete remediation steps
5) valid-annotation-format (format of @story/@req) - Rule: src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts - meta.messages: - invalidStoryFormat = "Invalid annotation format: {{details}}." - invalidReqFormat = "Invalid annotation format: {{details}}." - buildStoryErrorMessage(kind, value) and buildReqErrorMessage(kind, value) generate detailed messages about missing/invalid paths or IDs with example values - validateStoryAnnotation and validateReqAnnotation report via context.report({ messageId: 'invalidStoryFormat'/'invalidReqFormat', data: { details: } }) - Functions normalizeCommentLine, processComment, etc. guard against malformed comments and multi-line cases - Tests: tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts - Header references story 007.0 with error-message consistency REQs - Invalid tests assert both messageId and a precise details string, e.g.: - data.details = 'Missing story path for @story annotation. Expected an identifier like "REQ-EXAMPLE" (uppercase letters, numbers, and dashes only).' - Combined with the message template, final ESLint messages follow the convention "Invalid annotation format: {{details}}."
6) valid-story-reference (story file existence & paths) - Rule: src/rules/valid-story-reference.ts - meta.messages: - fileMissing: "Story file '{{path}}' not found" - invalidExtension: "Invalid story file extension for '{{path}}', expected '.story.md'" - invalidPath: "Invalid story path '{{path}}'" - fileAccessError: "Could not validate story file '{{path}}' due to a filesystem error: {{error}}. 7) valid-req-reference (requirement existence in story files) - Rule: src/rules/valid-req-reference.ts - meta.messages: - reqMissing: "Requirement '{{reqId}}' not found in '{{storyPath}}'" - invalidPath: "Invalid story path '{{storyPath}}'" - validateReqLine(...) parses @req lines, validates storyPath (no traversal/absolute), loads and caches story content, collects REQ- IDs, and reports via these messages including reqId and storyPath in data - Tests: tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts - Header references story 007.0 and the relevant error-reporting REQs - Invalid cases assert both messageId and full data payload: - { messageId: 'reqMissing', data: { reqId: 'REQ-NON-EXISTENT', storyPath: 'docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md' } } - { messageId: 'invalidPath', data: { storyPath: '../docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md' } }

9) Targeted tests for this story's suite - Command executed: npm test -- --ci --no-watchAll --runInBand --verbose --testPathPatterns tests/rules/error-reporting.test.ts - Output shows Jest invocation for that file with no reported failures, indicating the dedicated error-reporting tests run successfully.
traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and detailed requirements in docs/stories/007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING.story.md are implemented and verified:
- Core functionality and specificity: Every relevant rule (require-story-annotation, require-req-annotation, require-branch-annotation, valid-annotation-format, valid-story-reference, valid-req-reference) uses explicit meta.messages with placeholders ({{functionName}}, {{missing}}, {{details}}, {{path}}, {{reqId}}, {{storyPath}}) and surfaces these via context.report with well-structured data. Tests assert both messageId and data for all major cases. - ESLint best practices and integration: Messages are defined via meta.messages and referred to by messageId, with data placeholders, suggestions, and fixers in the idiomatic ESLint style. Helper functions handle context.report calls consistently and attach fixes/suggestions where appropriate. - User experience: Errors identify the precise function/branch/path/requirement, give clear descriptions of what is wrong, and often include concrete example fixes or automatically applied fixes (e.g., suggested @story/@req comments or normalized story paths). Branch and function location nodes are chosen so that the error underlines a meaningful identifier. - Error handling and incomplete context: All the helper logic around annotation detection, comment parsing, and filesystem access is defensive; exceptions are caught and converted to diagnostics (e.g., fileAccessError) rather than crashing. Guards around missing loc/range/sourceCode prevent failures when context is incomplete. - Consistency and severity: Message formats follow the patterns specified in the story (e.g., "Branch is missing required annotation: {{missing}}.", "Invalid annotation format: {{details}}.", clear file and requirement templates). The plugin’s exported configs map missing annotations and missing references to errors, and format issues to warnings, matching the severity conventions in the specification. - Traceability and testing: Every rule and helper includes @story annotations referencing this story where it influences error reporting, and multiple test files explicitly list this story and its REQs in their headers. The dedicated tests in tests/rules/error-reporting.test.ts confirm that the enhanced error messaging behavior for require-story-annotation works exactly as described.
Based on the implemented rules, helper functions, severity mapping, and comprehensive automated tests, the 007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING story is fully satisfied.
